        reminder = task.reminders.get()
        assert reminder.kind == FamilyTaskReminder.Kind.EVENT_REMINDER
        assert reminder.remind_at == event.end_time - timedelta(minutes=30)

    def test_clearing_event_unlinks_and_clears_derived_due(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        event = _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))
        task = _make_task(family, user)
        client = self._login(user)

        # First link it.
        client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(family, linked_event=str(event.pk)),
        )
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id == event.id

        # Now submit with no event selected -> unlink.
        resp = client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(family, linked_event=""),
        )

        assert resp.status_code == 302
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id is None
        assert task.linked_event_anchor == ""
        assert task.due_at is None
        assert not task.reminders.filter(
            kind=FamilyTaskReminder.Kind.EVENT_REMINDER
        ).exists()

    def test_linking_completed_task_warns_without_500(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        event = _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))
        task = _make_task(family, user)
        task.status = FamilyTask.Status.COMPLETED
        task.save(update_fields=["status"])
        client = self._login(user)

        resp = client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(
                family,
                status=FamilyTask.Status.COMPLETED,
                linked_event=str(event.pk),
            ),
            follow=True,
        )

        assert resp.status_code == 200
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id is None
        messages = [m.level_tag for m in resp.context["messages"]]
        assert "warning" in messages

So any save of a previously weakly-linked task silently upgrades it and discards the user-set due date. It may be *intended* (it aligns with "due date IS the event"), but right now it's an accident, not a decision, and no test pins it. Verify: create a task via `event_task_create`, POST the edit form with the same event still selected, assert what happens to `due_at`. Then decide — keep the conversion (and test it) or guard it (only re-link when the event field actually changed).

    )
    max_interval_hours = forms.IntegerField(
        required=False,
        min_value=1,
        label="Maximum interval",
        widget=forms.NumberInput(attrs={"class": "form-control", "min": "1"}),
    )
    is_as_needed = forms.BooleanField(

        widget=forms.Select(attrs={"class": "form-select"}),
    )
    linked_event_offset_minutes = forms.IntegerField(
        required=False,
        min_value=-525600,
        max_value=525600,
        label="Reminder offset (minutes)",
        help_text=(

            "positive = remind after). The due date is the event itself."
        ),
        widget=forms.NumberInput(attrs={"class": "form-control"}),
    )

    class Meta:
        model = FamilyTask
        fields = [

    def __init__(self, *args: Any, user: Any = None, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.user = user
        self.fields["notes"].required = False
        self.fields["due_at"].required = False
        self.fields["due_window_start_at"].required = False
        self.fields["due_window_end_at"].required = False
        self.fields["assigned_to"].required = False
        self.fields["task_kind"].required = False
        self.fields["series_is_active"].initial = True

        if self.instance and self.instance.pk:
            series = self.instance.task_series
            if series is not None:
                self.fields["medication_name"].initial = series.medication_name
                self.fields["dosage_text"].initial = series.dosage_text
                self.fields["instructions"].initial = series.instructions
                self.fields["min_interval_hours"].initial = series.min_interval_hours
                self.fields["max_interval_hours"].initial = series.max_interval_hours
                self.fields["is_as_needed"].initial = series.is_as_needed
                self.fields["series_is_active"].initial = series.is_active
            if user is not None:
                reminders_field = self.fields["reminders_enabled"]
                reminders_field.initial = self.instance.reminders.filter(
                    user=user
                ).exists()

            # Prefill the event-link fields from the existing task.
            if self.instance.linked_event_id:
                self.fields["linked_event"].initial = self.instance.linked_event_id
                self.fields["linked_event_anchor"].initial = (
                    self.instance.linked_event_anchor or FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END
                )
                self.fields[
                    "linked_event_offset_minutes"
                ].initial = self.instance.linked_event_offset_minutes

        if user:
            user_families = FamilyGroup.objects.filter(
                memberships__user=user, memberships__is_active=True
            )
            self.fields["family"].queryset = user_families  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

            # Scope assigned_to to active family members of the user's families
            family_user_ids = FamilyMembership.objects.filter(
                family__in=user_families, is_active=True
            ).values_list("user_id", flat=True)
            self.fields["assigned_to"].queryset = User.objects.filter(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                id__in=family_user_ids
            ).order_by("first_name", "username")
            # Show a friendly name instead of the raw username in the dropdown.
            self.fields["assigned_to"].label_from_instance = (  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                lambda member: member.get_full_name() or member.username
            )

            # Scope selectable events to ones the user can see in their families,
            # via the security-aware manager (mirrors organize/api.py link_event).
            event_qs = (

            self.fields["linked_event"].queryset = event_qs  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

            )

            # Default to the user's immediate family for new tasks
            if self.instance._state.adding:
                immediate = user_families.filter(group_type__type="IMMEDIATE").first()
                if immediate:
                    self.initial["family"] = immediate.pk

    def clean(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        cleaned_data = super().clean()
        if cleaned_data is None:
            return {}
        min_interval = cleaned_data.get("min_interval_hours")
        max_interval = cleaned_data.get("max_interval_hours")
        if min_interval and max_interval and max_interval < min_interval:
            self.add_error(
                "max_interval_hours",
                "Maximum interval must be greater than or equal to minimum interval.",
            )

        # The event must belong to the same family as the task, or the link
        # service guard (organize/services.py) would reject it generically.
        linked_event = cleaned_data.get("linked_event")
        family = cleaned_data.get("family")
        if (
            linked_event is not None
            and family is not None
            and linked_event.family_group_id != family.id
        ):
            self.add_error(
                "linked_event",
                "Pick an event from the selected family.",
            )
        return cleaned_data

    def apply_event_link(self, task: FamilyTask) -> str | None:
        """Link/unlink the task to an event via the shared service.

        Must run after the task is persisted (the service needs a saved task
        with a PK and a matching family). Returns an error message on failure,
        or ``None`` on success.
        """
        event = self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event")
        if event is None:
            if task.linked_event_id:
                unlink_task_from_event(task=task)
            return None
        try:
            link_task_to_event(
                task=task,
                event=event,
                anchor=(
                    self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event_anchor")
                    or FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END
                ),
                offset_minutes=self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event_offset_minutes"),
                reminder_user=self.user,
                created_by=self.user,
            )
        except TaskEventLinkError as exc:
            return exc.detail
        return None

    def save(self, commit: bool = True) -> FamilyTask:
        task = super().save(commit=commit)
        if commit and task.task_kind == FamilyTask.TaskKind.MEDICATION:
            update_medication_task_details(
                task=task,
                reminder_user=self.user,
                medication_name=self.cleaned_data.get("medication_name", ""),
                dosage_text=self.cleaned_data.get("dosage_text", ""),
                instructions=self.cleaned_data.get("instructions", ""),
                min_interval_hours=self.cleaned_data.get("min_interval_hours"),
                max_interval_hours=self.cleaned_data.get("max_interval_hours"),
                is_as_needed=self.cleaned_data.get("is_as_needed", False),
                is_active=self.cleaned_data.get("series_is_active", False),
                reminders_enabled=self.cleaned_data.get("reminders_enabled", False),
            )
        return task

"""Tests for the web Task form/views: friendly assignee labels and event linking.

These cover the browser-facing form (FamilyTaskWebForm) and the task_create /
task_edit views, which surface the same event-link service that mobile uses via
the API. The reminder/due-date derivation itself is covered in test_event_link.py;
here we verify the web form wiring (labels, scoping, link/unlink, error handling).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Any

import pytest
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.forms import ModelChoiceField
from django.test import Client
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils import timezone

from events.models import Event
from organize.models import FamilyTask, FamilyTaskReminder
from organize.services import create_task_from_household_action
from organize.web_forms import FamilyTaskWebForm
from users.models import FamilyGroup, FamilyMembership


def _setup_family(name: str = "Web Family") -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    family = FamilyGroup.objects.create(name=name)
    user = User.objects.create_user(
        username=f"{name}-admin",
        password="pass",  # pragma: allowlist secret
    )
    FamilyMembership.objects.create(
        user=user, family=family, role="PARENT", is_admin=True
    )
    profile = user.profile
    profile.primary_family = family
    profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
    family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
    family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
    return family, user


def _make_event(family: FamilyGroup, user: User, *, start_delta: timedelta) -> Event:
    start = timezone.now() + start_delta
    return Event.objects.create(
        title="Soccer game",
        start_time=start,
        end_time=start + timedelta(hours=2),
        creator=user,
        family_group=family,
        visibility="PUBLIC",
    )


def _make_task(family: FamilyGroup, user: User, **kwargs: Any) -> FamilyTask:
    return create_task_from_household_action(
        family=family,
        title=kwargs.pop("title", "Pick up a trash can"),
        source_client_app="organize",
        created_by=user,
        assigned_to=kwargs.pop("assigned_to", user),
        **kwargs,
    )


def _post_data(family: FamilyGroup, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data: dict[str, Any] = {
        "title": "Pick up a trash can",
        "family": str(family.pk),
        "status": FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
        "task_kind": FamilyTask.TaskKind.MANUAL,
        "notes": "",
        "linked_event_anchor": FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END,
    }
    data.update(overrides)
    return data


@pytest.mark.django_db
class TestAssigneeLabel:
    def test_full_name_used_when_present(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        user.first_name = "Daniel"
        user.last_name = "O'Brien"
        user.save(update_fields=["first_name", "last_name"])

        form = FamilyTaskWebForm(user=user)
        field = form.fields["assigned_to"]
        assert isinstance(field, ModelChoiceField)

        assert field.label_from_instance(user) == "Daniel O'Brien"

    def test_falls_back_to_username_when_no_name(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()

        form = FamilyTaskWebForm(user=user)
        field = form.fields["assigned_to"]
        assert isinstance(field, ModelChoiceField)

        assert field.label_from_instance(user) == user.username


@pytest.mark.django_db
class TestLinkedEventScoping:
    def test_queryset_excludes_events_from_other_families(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family("Mine")
        mine = _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))

        other_family, other_user = _setup_family("Theirs")
        theirs = _make_event(other_family, other_user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))

        form = FamilyTaskWebForm(user=user)
        field = form.fields["linked_event"]
        assert isinstance(field, ModelChoiceField)
        assert field.queryset is not None
        event_ids = set(field.queryset.values_list("id", flat=True))

        assert mine.id in event_ids
        assert theirs.id not in event_ids

    def test_clean_rejects_event_from_different_family(self) -> None:
        family_a, user = _setup_family("Alpha")
        family_b = FamilyGroup.objects.create(name="Beta")
        FamilyMembership.objects.create(
            user=user, family=family_b, role="PARENT", is_admin=True
        )
        family_b.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
        family_b.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
        event_b = _make_event(family_b, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))

        # Task assigned to family A, but the picked event belongs to family B.
        form = FamilyTaskWebForm(
            data=_post_data(family_a, linked_event=str(event_b.pk)),
            user=user,
        )

        assert not form.is_valid()
        assert "linked_event" in form.errors


@pytest.mark.django_db
class TestTaskEditEventLinking:
    def _login(self, user: User) -> Client:
        client = Client()
        client.force_login(user)
        return client

    def test_edit_page_renders_event_section(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))
        task = _make_task(family, user)
        client = self._login(user)

        resp = client.get(reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]))

        assert resp.status_code == 200
        assert b"Linked Event" in resp.content
        assert b"linked-event-fields" in resp.content

    def test_linking_via_edit_sets_due_at_and_reminder(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        event = _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))
        task = _make_task(family, user)
        client = self._login(user)

        resp = client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(
                family,
                linked_event=str(event.pk),
                linked_event_anchor=FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END,
                linked_event_offset_minutes="-30",
            ),
        )

        assert resp.status_code == 302
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id == event.id
        assert task.linked_event_anchor == FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END
        assert task.due_at == event.end_time

        reminder = task.reminders.get()
        assert reminder.kind == FamilyTaskReminder.Kind.EVENT_REMINDER
        assert reminder.remind_at == event.end_time - timedelta(minutes=30)

    def test_clearing_event_unlinks_and_clears_derived_due(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        event = _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))
        task = _make_task(family, user)
        client = self._login(user)

        # First link it.
        client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(family, linked_event=str(event.pk)),
        )
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id == event.id

        # Now submit with no event selected -> unlink.
        resp = client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(family, linked_event=""),
        )

        assert resp.status_code == 302
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id is None
        assert task.linked_event_anchor == ""
        assert task.due_at is None
        assert not task.reminders.filter(
            kind=FamilyTaskReminder.Kind.EVENT_REMINDER
        ).exists()

    def test_linking_completed_task_warns_without_500(self) -> None:
        family, user = _setup_family()
        event = _make_event(family, user, start_delta=timedelta(days=1))
        task = _make_task(family, user)
        task.status = FamilyTask.Status.COMPLETED
        task.save(update_fields=["status"])
        client = self._login(user)

        resp = client.post(
            reverse("organize_task_edit", args=[task.id]),
            data=_post_data(
                family,
                status=FamilyTask.Status.COMPLETED,
                linked_event=str(event.pk),
            ),
            follow=True,
        )

        assert resp.status_code == 200
        task.refresh_from_db()
        assert task.linked_event_id is None
        messages = [m.level_tag for m in resp.context["messages"]]
        assert "warning" in messages

Done. Both issues fixed, mobile-parity behavior, 123 organize tests pass, mypy + lint + django check clean.

## What changed

**1. Assign To shows username** → `organize/web_forms.py`: set `label_from_instance` on `assigned_to` → `get_full_name() or username`. Friendly name now, username fallback when blank.

**2. No event link** (the real ask — task ties to event as due date, mobile already has it): the backend already had `FamilyTask.linked_event` + the `link_task_to_event`/`unlink_task_from_event` service. Web form never surfaced it. Added:

- **`organize/web_forms.py`** — three fields: `linked_event` (picker, scoped via `Event.secure.for_user` to user's families), `linked_event_anchor` (start/end), `linked_event_offset_minutes` (reminder lead/lag). Plus `clean()` family-match guard, edit prefill, and `apply_event_link()` helper that calls the shared service with an **idempotency guard** (no reminder churn on unrelated edits; bare FK links upgrade to anchored).
- **`organize/web_views.py`** — `task_create`/`task_edit` call `apply_event_link` after save; link failure → warning + redirect (PRG, no dup tasks).
- **`templates/organize/task_form.html`** — Linked Event section + JS that greys the manual Due At when an event is linked.
- **`organize/test_task_web_form.py`** — 11 tests: labels, family scoping, link/unlink, reminder offset, idempotency, weak→strong upgrade, create-with-link, completed-task error path, template render.

## Semantics (confirmed with you)
Due date = the event's start/end exactly. The **offset shifts the reminder** (negative = before, positive = after) — matches mobile's `/link-event`. No service change, so no mobile drift.

## Note
Reverse direction (event → its tasks) already works — `event_detail.html` lists `event.organize_tasks`. The Due At JS toggle is progressive enhancement, asserted only at HTML level (test client runs no JS); degrades gracefully if it errors. Want it browser-verified, run `/verify` or Playwright on the edit page.

Nothing committed — changes are in the working tree.

---
name: clancal-timezone-safety
description: Use when changing ClanCal date, time, calendar sync, trip window, household due date, reminder, notification, widget, or API boundary behavior.
---

# ClanCal Timezone Safety

## Overview

ClanCal has three different concepts that must stay separate: instants, local calendar days, and source-local event times. Most timezone bugs come from converting one into another too early.

## Core Rules

- Instants: store and compare aware datetimes. Backend code should prefer `django.utils.timezone.now()` and API timestamps with offsets.
- Local calendar days: use `timezone.localdate(...)` on backend, or an explicit local date helper on mobile. Do not derive a user-facing day from `toISOString().split("T")[0]`.
- Date-only strings: parse `YYYY-MM-DD` as local midnight by splitting year/month/day, not with JavaScript `new Date(value)`.
- Source-local event times: when parsing Google, Apple, ICS, NPS, region, CSV, or scraped event times, choose the provider/user/region timezone explicitly before `make_aware`.
- Day windows: build inclusive/exclusive local boundaries in the intended timezone, then query datetimes. Avoid `__date` filters on `DateTimeField` unless the active DB timezone is deliberately the desired one.

## Backend Checks

- Avoid `datetime.now()`, `datetime.utcnow()`, `datetime.today()`, `date.today()`, and `datetime.fromtimestamp(...)` without `tz=`.
- Treat `timezone.now().date()` as suspicious in product behavior. It answers "today in the server/default timezone," not necessarily the family, trip, region, or device day.
- Avoid one-argument `timezone.make_aware(...)` for imported or user-entered event times; pass `ZoneInfo(...)` or another explicit timezone.
- Prefer `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` over `pytz` in new code.

## Mobile Checks

- Do not use `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` for trip, household, warranty, purchase, due, or filter dates.
- Use existing helpers such as `parseTripDate` for trip dates; add similarly named helpers for other date-only domains before duplicating parser logic.
- `Date.now()` and `new Date().toISOString()` are fine for cache stamps, IDs, optimistic `created_at`, and true instants.

## Tests

Cover at least one timezone west of UTC and one east of UTC for date-only behavior. Include a DST boundary when event windows, recurrence, or reminders are involved.

        """Link/unlink the task to an event via the shared service.

        Must run after the task is persisted (the service needs a saved task
        with a PK and a matching family). Returns an error message on failure,
        or ``None`` on success.
        """
        event = self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event")
        if event is None:
            if task.linked_event_id:
                unlink_task_from_event(task=task)
            return None

        anchor = (
            self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event_anchor") or FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END
        )
        # The service stores 0 when no offset is supplied.
        offset = self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event_offset_minutes") or 0

        # Idempotency: skip re-linking (which would re-create the reminder) when
        # the task already carries this exact derived link. Without this, every
        # unrelated edit of a linked task would churn its reminder. A bare FK
        # link (anchor == "") deliberately fails this check, so saving the form
        # upgrades it to a proper anchored link with a derived due date/reminder.

            task.linked_event_id == event.id
            and task.linked_event_anchor == anchor
            and (task.linked_event_offset_minutes or 0) == offset
        )
        if already_linked:
            return None

            link_task_to_event(
                task=task,
                event=event,
                anchor=anchor,
                offset_minutes=offset,
                reminder_user=self.user,
                created_by=self.user,
            )
        except TaskEventLinkError as exc:
            return exc.detail
        return None

    def apply_event_link(self, task: FamilyTask) -> str | None:
        """Link/unlink the task to an event via the shared service.

        Must run after the task is persisted (the service needs a saved task
        with a PK and a matching family). Returns an error message on failure,
        or ``None`` on success.
        """
        event = self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event")
        if event is None:
            if task.linked_event_id:
                unlink_task_from_event(task=task)
            return None

        anchor = (
            self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event_anchor") or FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END
        )
        # The service stores 0 when no offset is supplied.
        offset = self.cleaned_data.get("linked_event_offset_minutes") or 0

        # Idempotency: skip re-linking (which would re-create the reminder) when
        # the task already carries this exact derived link. Without this, every
        # unrelated edit of a linked task would churn its reminder. A bare FK
        # link (anchor == "") deliberately fails this check, so saving the form
        # upgrades it to a proper anchored link with a derived due date/reminder.
        already_linked = (
            task.linked_event_id == event.id
            and task.linked_event_anchor == anchor
            and (task.linked_event_offset_minutes or 0) == offset
        )
        if already_linked:
            return None

                task=task,
                event=event,
                anchor=anchor,
                offset_minutes=offset,
                reminder_user=self.user,
                created_by=self.user,
            )
        except TaskEventLinkError as exc:
            return exc.detail

def _setup_family(name: str = "Web Family") -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    family = FamilyGroup.objects.create(name=name)
    user = User.objects.create_user(
        username=f"{name}-admin",
        password="pass",  # pragma: allowlist secret
    )
    FamilyMembership.objects.create(
        user=user, family=family, role="PARENT", is_admin=True
    )
    profile = user.profile
    profile.primary_family = family
    profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
    family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
    family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
    return family, user


def _make_event(family: FamilyGroup, user: User, *, start_delta: timedelta) -> Event:
    start = timezone.now() + start_delta
    return Event.objects.create(
        title="Soccer game",
        start_time=start,
        end_time=start + timedelta(hours=2),
        creator=user,
        family_group=family,
        visibility="PUBLIC",
    )


def _make_task(family: FamilyGroup, user: User, **kwargs: Any) -> FamilyTask:
    return create_task_from_household_action(
        family=family,
        title=kwargs.pop("title", "Pick up a trash can"),
        source_client_app="organize",
        created_by=user,
        assigned_to=kwargs.pop("assigned_to", user),
        **kwargs,
    )


def _post_data(family: FamilyGroup, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data: dict[str, Any] = {
        "title": "Pick up a trash can",
        "family": str(family.pk),
        "status": FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
        "task_kind": FamilyTask.TaskKind.MANUAL,
        "notes": "",
        "linked_event_anchor": FamilyTask.EventAnchor.END,
    }
    data.update(overrides)
    return data

125 pass, mypy + lint clean. Done.

## What changed

**Too-far-future fix** — `organize/web_forms.py`: bounded the event queryset to `[now − 1 day, now + 365 days]` (aware-instant `timezone.now()`, no naive/`__date` — timezone-safe) and ordered **soonest-first** instead of furthest-first. Recurring birthdays no longer dump 2054 occurrences at the top. The currently-linked event is unioned in so it stays selectable even if it falls outside the window when editing.

**Wrong-looking times fix** — dates now render via the `|date` template filter (active timezone) instead of an f-string that printed the UTC-stored value. The "4:00 AM" birthdays will show in local time.

**Card selection UI** — `templates/organize/task_form.html`: replaced the native `<select>` with a scrollable list of selectable cards (radio-backed, fully accessible: `role="radiogroup"`, hidden native radios, keyboard focus ring). Each card shows the event **title** (bold) + **formatted date/time** (muted), a check icon on the selected one, hover/selected states using the app's `--primary`/`--primary-light` tokens. A "No linked event" card at the top unlinks. Updated the Due At greying JS to read the radio group.

**Tests** — `organize/test_task_web_form.py`: added window-excludes-far-future, linked-far-future-stays-selectable, and strengthened the render test to assert the card markup. 13 form/view tests, 125 organize total.

Card states:
```

│ ○  No linked event                          │   ← unlink
│    Task keeps its own due date              │
```

content.text:
Confirmed the mobile wiring: `OrganizeTaskDetailScreen` mounts `EventPicker` and opens it from the "Link event" button. I have a complete picture for both apps.

---

## Investigation complete — task↔event link picker

### MOBILE (`/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/mobile`) — Expo/React Native

**1. Yes, full task→event link UI exists.**
- Picker UI: `src/components/organize/EventPicker.tsx`
- Mounted/opened from: `src/screens/organize/OrganizeTaskDetailScreen.tsx:492` (modal), triggered by the "Link event" button at `:443-445`; unlink at `:220-233`.
- API: `src/api/organize.ts:172` `linkTaskToEvent` → `POST /organize/tasks/{id}/link-event/`; `:180` `unlinkTaskFromEvent` → `POST /organize/tasks/{id}/unlink-event/`. Reverse list param wired at `src/api/organize.ts:97-98` (`linked_event`).
- Payload schema (anchor START/END, offset_minutes): `src/api/schemas/organize.schema.ts:597-608`.

**2. How it lists the events you pick from — already bounded and tight.**
`EventPicker.tsx:51-69` `loadEvents`:
```
const now = new Date();
const end = new Date(now.getTime());
end.setDate(end.getDate() + 30);
eventsApi.getEvents({ start_date: toDateParam(now), end_date: toDateParam(end), search: ... })
```
The list is bounded to **[today, today+30 days]** — far tighter than the web's [now-1d, now+365d]. So the "recurring birthdays out to 2054" explosion cannot happen here. `getEvents` (`src/api/events.ts:121`) passes those dates to `/events/` and relies on backend default ordering (it sets no explicit `ordering` param, same as the web form did). Empty state literally says "No upcoming events in the next 30 days" (`:163`).

**3. Date display — local TZ, correct.** `formatEventTime` (`EventPicker.tsx:35-42`) uses `new Date(iso).toLocaleString(...)` → renders in device-local time. No UTC bug.

**4. Bottom line (mobile): Already handles it. No fix needed.** It has an even stricter window than the web fix. The only minor difference from the web fix is it doesn't pass an explicit soonest-first `ordering` param, but a 30-day window can't produce 2054 occurrences regardless.

---

### DESKTOP (`/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/desktop`) — Electron (`clancal-desktop`, Vite + React renderer)

**1. No task→event link picker UI exists.**
- There is **no `linkTaskToEvent`/`unlinkTaskFromEvent`** method and **no call to `link-event`/`unlink-event` endpoints** anywhere (verified by search — zero hits).
- `linked_event` is only ever set programmatically:
  - `src/renderer/lib/api.ts:1213` (`createTask`) and `:1229` (`updateTask`) accept an optional `linked_event` string in the PATCH/POST body.
  - The only caller that sets it is the legacy Clancy AI draft-suggestion flow: `src/renderer/_legacy/App.legacy.tsx:1137-1138`, which pulls a pre-supplied event ID from the AI suggestion payload — not from a user-browsable event list.
  - The active task UI (`src/renderer/components/tasks/TasksSurface.tsx:89-129`) creates/updates tasks with only `title/notes/due_at/status` — `linked_event` isn't even in its input types.
- Other `linked_event` references are read-only display (famstream "From event" labels: `src/renderer/components/famstream/FamStreamScreen.tsx:232-241`) and the reverse-list filter `listTasks({eventId})` → `linked_event` query param (`src/renderer/lib/api.ts:1136-1137`).

**2. Event listing (for completeness).** `listEvents` (`src/renderer/lib/api.ts:1697`) has *optional* `start_date`/`end_date` filters with no auto-window, but it does **not feed any task-link picker** — it backs the calendar/today surfaces. So the unbounded concern is moot for the linking feature.

**3. Date display.** `TodaySurface.tsx:274` uses `toLocaleTimeString` (local TZ). No relevant UTC issue, and no link-picker dates to render anyway.

**4. Bottom line (desktop): No such feature.** There is no user-facing "pick an event to link this task" picker, so there is nothing with the events-list window/ordering problem to fix. The web fix has no desktop counterpart.

---

### Summary table

| App | Task→event link picker? | Event list window | Ordering | TZ display | Needs the web fix? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile | Yes (`EventPicker.tsx`) | Bounded [now, now+30d] | backend default (no explicit param) | Local (`toLocaleString`) | **No — already handled, tighter than web** |
| Desktop | **No picker UI** (only programmatic `linked_event` via AI drafts) | N/A to linking | N/A | Local | **No — feature doesn't exist** |

Neither app shares the "events go to 2054 / unbounded / badly ordered" problem you fixed on the web backend. Mobile already constrains to a 30-day window; desktop has no link-picker at all.

Confirmed the mobile wiring: `OrganizeTaskDetailScreen` mounts `EventPicker` and opens it from the "Link event" button. I have a complete picture for both apps.

---

## Investigation complete — task↔event link picker

### MOBILE (`/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/mobile`) — Expo/React Native

**1. Yes, full task→event link UI exists.**
- Picker UI: `src/components/organize/EventPicker.tsx`
- Mounted/opened from: `src/screens/organize/OrganizeTaskDetailScreen.tsx:492` (modal), triggered by the "Link event" button at `:443-445`; unlink at `:220-233`.
- API: `src/api/organize.ts:172` `linkTaskToEvent` → `POST /organize/tasks/{id}/link-event/`; `:180` `unlinkTaskFromEvent` → `POST /organize/tasks/{id}/unlink-event/`. Reverse list param wired at `src/api/organize.ts:97-98` (`linked_event`).
- Payload schema (anchor START/END, offset_minutes): `src/api/schemas/organize.schema.ts:597-608`.

**2. How it lists the events you pick from — already bounded and tight.**
`EventPicker.tsx:51-69` `loadEvents`:
```
const now = new Date();
const end = new Date(now.getTime());
end.setDate(end.getDate() + 30);
eventsApi.getEvents({ start_date: toDateParam(now), end_date: toDateParam(end), search: ... })
```
The list is bounded to **[today, today+30 days]** — far tighter than the web's [now-1d, now+365d]. So the "recurring birthdays out to 2054" explosion cannot happen here. `getEvents` (`src/api/events.ts:121`) passes those dates to `/events/` and relies on backend default ordering (it sets no explicit `ordering` param, same as the web form did). Empty state literally says "No upcoming events in the next 30 days" (`:163`).

**3. Date display — local TZ, correct.** `formatEventTime` (`EventPicker.tsx:35-42`) uses `new Date(iso).toLocaleString(...)` → renders in device-local time. No UTC bug.

**4. Bottom line (mobile): Already handles it. No fix needed.** It has an even stricter window than the web fix. The only minor difference from the web fix is it doesn't pass an explicit soonest-first `ordering` param, but a 30-day window can't produce 2054 occurrences regardless.

---

### DESKTOP (`/Users/danobrien/code/family-schedule-app/desktop`) — Electron (`clancal-desktop`, Vite + React renderer)

**1. No task→event link picker UI exists.**
- There is **no `linkTaskToEvent`/`unlinkTaskFromEvent`** method and **no call to `link-event`/`unlink-event` endpoints** anywhere (verified by search — zero hits).
- `linked_event` is only ever set programmatically:
  - `src/renderer/lib/api.ts:1213` (`createTask`) and `:1229` (`updateTask`) accept an optional `linked_event` string in the PATCH/POST body.
  - The only caller that sets it is the legacy Clancy AI draft-suggestion flow: `src/renderer/_legacy/App.legacy.tsx:1137-1138`, which pulls a pre-supplied event ID from the AI suggestion payload — not from a user-browsable event list.
  - The active task UI (`src/renderer/components/tasks/TasksSurface.tsx:89-129`) creates/updates tasks with only `title/notes/due_at/status` — `linked_event` isn't even in its input types.
- Other `linked_event` references are read-only display (famstream "From event" labels: `src/renderer/components/famstream/FamStreamScreen.tsx:232-241`) and the reverse-list filter `listTasks({eventId})` → `linked_event` query param (`src/renderer/lib/api.ts:1136-1137`).

**2. Event listing (for completeness).** `listEvents` (`src/renderer/lib/api.ts:1697`) has *optional* `start_date`/`end_date` filters with no auto-window, but it does **not feed any task-link picker** — it backs the calendar/today surfaces. So the unbounded concern is moot for the linking feature.

**3. Date display.** `TodaySurface.tsx:274` uses `toLocaleTimeString` (local TZ). No relevant UTC issue, and no link-picker dates to render anyway.

**4. Bottom line (desktop): No such feature.** There is no user-facing "pick an event to link this task" picker, so there is nothing with the events-list window/ordering problem to fix. The web fix has no desktop counterpart.

---

### Summary table

| App | Task→event link picker? | Event list window | Ordering | TZ display | Needs the web fix? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile | Yes (`EventPicker.tsx`) | Bounded [now, now+30d] | backend default (no explicit param) | Local (`toLocaleString`) | **No — already handled, tighter than web** |
| Desktop | **No picker UI** (only programmatic `linked_event` via AI drafts) | N/A to linking | N/A | Local | **No — feature doesn't exist** |

Neither app shares the "events go to 2054 / unbounded / badly ordered" problem you fixed on the web backend. Mobile already constrains to a 30-day window; desktop has no link-picker at all.
